title: Finite-type quasi-coherent submodules exhaust a module on a qcqs space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Assume $X$ is quasi-compact, meaning it admits a representable surjective etale map from a quasi-compact scheme, and quasi-separated, meaning its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. For every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $M$ on the small etale site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], let $\Sigma(M)$ be the inclusion-ordered set of quasi-coherent submodules $N\subseteq M$ of finite type, where finite type means etale locally finitely generated. Take this set in a universe containing the subobjects of $M$ [def-weil-size-convention]. Then $\Sigma(M)$ is nonempty and directed, and the inclusions induce an isomorphism $$\varinjlim_{N\in\Sigma(M)}N\xrightarrow{\sim}M$$ in the category of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. No Noetherian or finite-type hypothesis on $M$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0829, lemma-directed-colimit-finite-type, statement and proof; nonempty directed indexing by subobjects is the first paragraph of the proof.

proof.text: The zero submodule belongs to $\Sigma(M)$: it has the empty presentation and no generators. For $N,P\in\Sigma(M)$, form $H=\operatorname{im}(N\oplus P\to M)$. By [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits], $N\oplus P$ and $H$ are quasi-coherent. On a common etale refinement where $N$ and $P$ have finite generating lists, their images together generate $H$: composing their surjection from a finite free module with the image quotient is still surjective. Hence $H$ is of finite type and contains both $N$ and $P$. Thus $\Sigma(M)$ is nonempty and directed.

source.place: Tag 0829, lemma-directed-colimit-finite-type, first paragraph of proof (with zero submodule made explicit).

proof.text: The quasi-compact atlas in the hypothesis makes $|X|$ quasi-compact: pull an open cover back to the atlas, choose a finite subcover there, and use surjectivity; continuity is part of the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. The absolute-diagonal hypothesis is exactly that of [lem-sfb-space-module-fp-directed-approximation]. Apply that node to obtain a small filtered diagram $F_j$ of finitely presented quasi-coherent modules with colimit maps $a_j:F_j\to M$. Put $G_j=\operatorname{im}(a_j)$. Its quasi-coherence follows from [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits]. Each local presentation $\mathcal O^m\to\mathcal O^n\to F_j\to0$ gives a surjection $\mathcal O^n\to G_j$ by composing with the image quotient. Consequently $G_j\in\Sigma(M)$.

source.place: Tags 0829 and 07V9, lemma-directed-colimit-finite-type, second paragraph, and lemma-colimit-finitely-presented.

proof.text: Use the small site skeleton and the universe containing the subobjects prescribed by [def-weil-size-convention]. By [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian], module sheaves form an abelian category with small colimits and exact filtered colimits. Set $C=\varinjlim_{N\in\Sigma(M)}N$ and write $\lambda_N:N\to C$ and $c:C\to M$ for the canonical maps. Apply exact filtered colimits to the compatible sequences $0\to N\to M\to M/N\to0$. The constant diagram with value $M$ has colimit $M$: all legs of any cocone agree because every two indices have a common upper bound. We therefore obtain an exact sequence $0\to C\xrightarrow{c}M\to\varinjlim_N(M/N)\to0$. In particular $c$ is a monomorphism.

source.place: Tags 03DA and 03DB, lemma-abelian and lemma-limits-colimits; explicit filtered-union interpretation of the last sentence of Tag 0829.

proof.text: Factor $a_j$ as $F_j\xrightarrow{q_j}G_j\hookrightarrow M$, and define $b_j=\lambda_{G_j}q_j:F_j\to C$. For every transition $t:F_j\to F_k$, the equality $a_k t=a_j$ implies $G_j\subseteq G_k$ and $q_k t=(G_j\hookrightarrow G_k)q_j$. Hence $b_k t=b_j$. The colimit property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] of the $a_j$ gives $b:M\to C$ with $ba_j=b_j$. For every $j$, $cba_j=c\lambda_{G_j}q_j=a_j$, so that same colimit property gives $cb=1_M$. Since $c$ is monic, $c(bc)=c$ implies $bc=1_C$. Thus the canonical map $c$ is an isomorphism, as required.

source.place: Tag 0829, lemma-directed-colimit-finite-type, final sentence; explicit cocone and inverse verification.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q29-5cac77974 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, its four steps, every cited statement and Stacks 0829 (spaces-limits.tex l.2302) in full. The statement and stmt_deps are unchanged from the base. There are no new nodes and no repair note, and clones/live and side-live both show the item unsplit, so no other group took it. Step 1: directedness uses images of N⊕P, which are quasi-coherent by the 03M1 node; finite type holds on a common étale refinement. Step 2: |X| is quasi-compact as the continuous image of the quasi-compact atlas under the final topology of def-a1-space-point-topology. Diagonal quasi-compactness on scheme tests implies it on affine tests, which is the 07V9 node's hypothesis; the step's word 'exactly' overstates this but is harmless. The G_j are of finite type via O^n↠F_j↠G_j. Step 3: on the small skeleton, lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian gives exact filtered colimits, so applying it to 0→N→M→M/N→0 makes c mono. Step 4: b comes from the cocone b_j=λ_{G_j}q_j; compatibility uses that the inclusions are mono, cb=1 by uniqueness and bc=1 because c is mono, and this holds for a non-poset filtered J. Edge cases checked: M=0, X empty, M of finite type. No duplicate nodes, no SGA citation. lean.statement: theorem finiteTypeQuasiCoherentSubmodules_colimit {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (hqc : ∃ (T : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj T ⟶ X.obj.obj), CompactSpace T.left ∧ IsEtale a ∧ IsSurjective a) (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated X) (M : X.Modules) [M.IsQuasicoherent] : Nonempty (finiteTypeQuasiCoherentSubmodules M) ∧ Directed (· ≤ ·) (fun N : (finiteTypeQuasiCoherentSubmodules M) ↦ N) ∧ ∃ (c : Cocone (finiteTypeQuasiCoherentSubmoduleDiagram M)) (h : c.pt = M), Nonempty (IsColimit c) ∧ ∀ N : (finiteTypeQuasiCoherentSubmodules M), c.ι.app N ≫ eqToHom h = N.val.arrow
lean.note: The subobject subtype and its canonical inclusion diagram are helpers of this statement. The colimit cocone has vertex equal to M and legs exactly the subobject arrows; equivalently the canonical colimit comparison to M is an isomorphism. Absolute quasi-separatedness uses the landed affine-test definition, with no separation hypothesis on S.

reviewed_lean.note: The Lean matches the node and Stacks 0829 clause by clause. Hypotheses: hqc is a quasi-compact étale surjective atlas (same form as the landed Tag 0853 extension lemma), hqs is the landed IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated (stmt_dep correctly added), and M is any quasi-coherent module with no extra assumption. Σ(M) is the subtype of Subobject M with Mathlib IsQuasicoherent ∧ IsFiniteType (site-local finite generators, i.e. étale locally finitely generated), in the universe of Subobject M. Conclusion: Nonempty, Directed in the subtype order, and the inclusion cocone with vertex M (legs N.val.arrow) is a colimit, equivalent to the canonical comparison being an isomorphism. The helpers have real data and docstrings, the proof is only sorry with the 4 steps in the docstring, and lean.statement matches the file verbatim. Edge cases M=0 and empty X are fine. No duplicate in Mathlib or lean/Sheaf. Not recompiled (worker compile evidence). No findings.
